João de Freitas da Silva raised a company of 100 men in Madeira at his own cost to fight in Pernambuco.
Filipe III approved the Misericórdia's own statutes.
A law established the meia anata tax.
A chapel of Nossa Senhora da Estrela is recorded in the Calhau parish.
The first works of the Pico fortress (Castelo de São João do Pico) in Funchal were completed; the date is inscribed over its outer gate.
The Funchal council recorded that St James the Less was credited with sparing Madeira from the pirates of 1617.
The Funchal council renewed its old vows to St James by a new deed, confirming Madeiran gratitude after grain relief and the building of a new chapel.
Bishop D. Jerónimo Fernando blessed the new chapel of St James in Funchal.

mentions.as_written: 25 do mês de Julho do mesmo ano

summary: Death of António da Silva Barreto.
Death of Manuel da Silva Câmara, holder of the Leme entail.
The Dutch attacked the Portuguese camp in Brazil; João Fernandes Vieira was captured and ransomed.
D. João de Meneses took office as governor-general of Madeira.
Manuel Tomás's poem Insulana, on Madeira, was published in Antwerp.
The chapel of São Lourenço was built inside the Funchal fortress, which then took its name; the date is inscribed over the chapel door.
The donativo war tax on the produce of the land was imposed in Madeira under Spanish rule, and is mentioned in municipal records until 1691.
The Jesuits acquired the Pico do Cardo property in Santo António.
A second lease of seafront land in Funchal was granted for a capstan.
An order was given to complete the main chapel of Funchal Cathedral.
Luís de Miranda Henriques Pinto was appointed governor-general of Madeira.
The church of Ponta Delgada was repaired and modified.
Luís de Miranda Henriques Pinto governed Madeira as the last governor-general under Spanish rule and completed the Pico castle.
Madeira was obliged to pay 10,000 cruzados yearly towards the fleet to recover Pernambuco, the levy falling first on the clergy.
Major repairs were made to the parish church of Porto da Cruz.
Manuel Dias de Andrade died in Cape Verde with a fleet bound to recover Pernambuco.
The people of Achadas da Cruz again petitioned unsuccessfully for a curacy.
Canon António Espranger Rocha entrusted the unfinished Mosteiro Novo to the bishop, D. Jerónimo Fernando.
A book of masses by Duarte Lobo, later held at Funchal Cathedral, was printed in Antwerp.
The parish church of Espírito Santo in Calheta was rebuilt.
Pedro da Silva died in India while serving as its governor.
From about 1640 English merchants settled in Madeira in greater numbers, taking over trade and promoting viticulture.
From 1640 until 1834 Madeira was administered by governors and captains-general, who replaced the governors-general.
Padre Francisco Valhadolid is said to have been born.
Fr. Gregório Batista died some time after 1640.
Works on the Pico fortress in Funchal continued until this year.
The taro Colocasia antiquorum is said to have been introduced to Madeira.
Luís de Miranda Henriques Pinto was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
Luís de Miranda Henriques Pinto took office as governor of Madeira.
At the end of December 1640 a ship from Cádiz brought Madeira vague news of events in Portugal.

The revolution of 1 December 1640 in Lisbon ended Castilian rule and gave the throne to the Duke of Bragança as D. João IV; Madeira and Porto Santo joined it with enthusiasm, and António Veloso de Lira led Portuguese students home from Salamanca.
Guilherme Acre was living on Porto Santo around 1640.
At the end of 1641 Bishop D. Jerónimo Fernando left for the mainland, never to return.
The Cortes decreed the finto war tax for three years.
Padre António Cordeiro was born in Angra.
D. João IV reformed the militia.
A caravel brought D. João IV's letters to the governor and the bishop of Madeira.
News of the Restoration reached Madeira and D. João IV was acclaimed king in the Funchal town hall, ending Castilian rule; the bishop helped calm the people.
A charter of D. João IV condemned the continued felling of mountain forests, harmful to rainfall and levadas.
Clergy, nobility and people in Funchal swore loyalty to D. João IV.
A Funchal crowd expelled Castilian and other officials, and Portuguese citizens replaced Spaniards in council offices.
Master Francisco Rodrigues Belo was ordered to ready a caravel for Lisbon.
The lepers' allowance at the São Lázaro hospital was raised to 40 réis.
Porto Santo received news of the Restoration and celebrated with salvoes, causing an Ottoman squadron of twelve sail that nearly blockaded the island to withdraw.
Envoys were elected to carry the Funchal council's letters to the king.
New councillors were elected so that the letters to the king could be signed.
The caravel carrying the envoys sailed for Lisbon.
Funchal voted a voluntary donation for the war with Castile.

mentions.as_written: 12 de Abril do mesmo ano de 1641

summary: Manuel Homem da Câmara was appointed first ouvidor of Machico.
A royal letter ordered the Funchal Câmara to assist the provedor da fazenda.
Nuno Pereira Freire was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
Padre José da Costa de Lima was appointed first chaplain of the chapel of the São Lourenço fortress, the earliest known such warrant.
A chapel of Nossa Senhora da Piedade was erected in Estreito da Calheta.
The office of sea alcaide on Porto Santo already existed well before 1642.
A third lease of seafront land in Funchal for a capstan was granted.
The governor ordered construction of the Ilhéu fortress.
Nuno Pereira Freire took office as the first post-Restoration governor of Madeira.
D. João IV ordered fleets to be supplied with Madeira wine.
Patacas, tostões and other coins were recorded in circulation in Madeira.
António Veloso de Lira's Espelho de Lusitanos was published.
Royal letters of 1644 and 1655 granted loans for improving springs and aqueducts (levadas) in Madeira.
An order was given to build a redoubt, a salient in the walls of the Funchal Customs House covering the beach, and it was built.
Jorge da Costa Osório investigated the murder of the corregedor Gaspar Mousinho.
Luís Telo de Meneses was killed at the battle of Montijo.
The customs judge of Santa Cruz was made deputy for the Funchal provedor.
A royal charter on irrigation water was issued.
The customs redoubt and its gates were completed under Governor Manuel de Sousa Mascarenhas, as dated by an inscription.
D. João IV granted the Agrela family the office of clerk of the Funchal council.
Manuel de Sousa Mascarenhas was appointed governor of Madeira, taking office on 11 April.
The Misericórdia complained to the king about the bad site of its hospital.
A decree gave Madeira a seat in the Cortes on the first bench.
An export duty of one cruzado (400 réis) per pipe of wine was established, when exports were about 2,000 pipes.
A regimento fixed the finto tax at 10 per cent of income.
The bishop allowed the founder's nephews and nieces to live in the Mosteiro Novo building.
Inácio da Câmara Leme married Isabel de Castelo Branco Bettencourt.
Manuel Lobo da Silva was appointed captain-general of Madeira on 21 October 1647 and took office in May 1648.
D. João de Meneses died in Holland.
With many Madeiran sugar mills already in ruins, a royal charter offered rewards and loans to rebuild them.
Birth of Francisco da Câmara Leme.
The founders signed the deed of endowment of the chapel of Nossa Senhora de Belém.
The stipend of the priest of Madalena do Mar was revised.
Gaspar Homem de El-Rei and D. Isabel Florença founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora das Mercês at Lombo das Mercês, Arco da Calheta.
The English merchant Perry was trading in Funchal.
Canon Henrique Calaça de Viveiros founded the Incarnação convent in Funchal.
Rafael Esteves built the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Desterro at Ledo e Vinhático, Arco da Calheta.
The original chapel of Santa Clara in Funchal was demolished and the church entirely rebuilt and enlarged.
Francisco Fernandes de Barros Maciel built the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Nazaré at Arco da Calheta.

mentions.as_written: terceiro ou ultimo quartel do século XVII

summary: Bishop D. Jerónimo Fernando died and was buried in the Graça convent, Lisbon.
A decree fixed the Porto do Moniz parish priest's stipend at 20$000 réis, a moio of wheat and a pipe of wine.
Captain Manuel de Figueiroa founded the chapel of São João Baptista at the Quinta de São João, Calheta.
Bartolomeu de Vasconcelos da Cunha was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira on 21 August 1651, taking office on 16 October.
A charter gave the Conde de Vimioso the sole right to buy and export laurel berries.
The first recolhidas entered the house of Santa Teresa de Jesus, forerunner of the Incarnação convent.
António Rodrigues Jardim founded a hermitage to the Souls in Purgatory in Ribeira Brava.
D. João IV granted the captaincy of Porto Santo to Vitorino Bettencourt Perestrelo.
D. Francisco Manuel de Melo's third Epanaphora, on the Machim discovery legend, is dated 1654.
Inácio da Câmara Leme rebuilt the chapel of São Filipe at the Quinta do Leme.
Fr. Remígio da Assunção died.
Under the treaty with England, British goods were admitted to Portugal at low duty.
Troilo de Vasconcelos da Cunha, son of the governor, was born in Funchal.
The fort of Nossa Senhora da Conceição do Ilhéu at Funchal was built, its inscription naming Governor Bartolomeu de Vasconcelos da Cunha.
Gaspar Berenguer de Andrade and his wife Isabel de França Andrade founded a house for recolhidas at Calheta, origin of the Convento das Mercês.
Simão Nunes Machado and his wife endowed the chapel of the Eleven Thousand Virgins in the Jesuit church of São João Evangelista.
A royal charter altered the stipend of the priest of Tábua.
A regimento removed all exemptions from the finto tax.
D. João IV granted Funchal representation in the Cortes.
According to the annotator of the Saudades, the Mosteiro Novo was begun around 1654.
Padre Francisco de Castro's Sermão da Visitação was printed at La Rochelle.
Pedro da Silva da Cunha was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
A royal charter concerning irrigation water in Madeira was issued.
The fleet carrying D. Francisco Manuel de Melo into exile left Lisbon, reaching Madeira four days later.
Pedro da Silva da Cunha took office as governor of Madeira.
The fleet carrying D. Francisco Manuel de Melo left Madeira for Cabo Verde.
Benedito Catalão was appointed lieutenant of the Castelo de São João do Pico.
Cidrão signed the first deed donating property to found the Recolhimento do Bom Jesus.
Diogo Bernardes Branco built the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Incarnação at Louros.
João Bettencourt de Atouguia founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora de Jesus.
The chapel of Nossa Senhora do Livramento at Ponta do Sol was built and endowed, with an entail instituted (deed of 14 September).
A letter from Queen Luísa de Gusmão announced the death of D. João IV to Funchal.
The 6th Count of Vimioso died in a quarrel.
Padre Francisco de Castro's Sermão da Conceição was printed at La Rochelle.
The Carmo church in Funchal was built, begun in 1656 and completed in 1660.
Building of the Ilhéu fortress (Nossa Senhora da Conceição) off Funchal began.
The Piedade chapel at Vargem de Baixo, Calheta, was built.
Endowment deed of the Maravilhas chapel founded by Diogo Bettencourt Correia and his wife Catarina da Silva.
The chapel of Nossa Senhora da Pena was built and endowed by public deed by its founders.
Gaspar Betencourt de Andrade founded a chapel in São Pedro, Funchal.
The captain-general assembled Madeira's councils in Funchal to regularise payment of the donativo for the War of Restoration.
Domingos Rodrigues built the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Carmo in Campanário.
The English consulate in Madeira was created, first held by João Cater.
The house that became the Convento das Mercês was turned into a religious recolhimento under a rule.
The deed of endowment of the Saúde chapel in São Pedro was signed.
Diogo de Mendonça Furtado was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
Manuel Ribeiro Neto's canon-law pleadings on Funchal church matters were published in one volume.
The Anglo-Portuguese royal marriage of D. Catarina de Bragança and Carlos II led to large-scale Madeira wine exports by English merchants, who enjoyed tax exemption on them from 1660 to 1662.
Canon Domingos Gonçalves de Alvarenga erected the chapel of São João Baptista in Santana.
The house of the Incarnação became a Poor Clare convent and its founder donated his property to it.
The new parish church of Porto do Moniz was built.
Hans Sloane, later a visitor to Madeira, was born in Ireland.
Matias de Mendonça e Vasconcelos erected a Rosary chapel in Machico.
D. Francisco Manuel de Melo's third «Epanafora», telling the Machim legend of Madeira's discovery, was first published.
Bartolomeu João de Abreu was granted his father's office of fortificador.
A royal charter ordered protective walls to be built on the Ribeira Brava.

Madeira was granted to Infanta D. Catarina de Bragança by royal warrant of 23 November 1660 (procuration dated 18 November), and Governor Furtado presented the donation deed to the Funchal council for registration on 7 December; it was also registered at Machico.
Diogo de Mendonça Furtado took office as governor of Madeira.
The English merchant Ricardo Jarvis settled in Funchal, founding the Jérvis family.
A flood almost completely destroyed the parish church of São Jorge at Calhau.
Honorato Sauvaire came to Madeira as French consul.
A chapel of Nossa Senhora dos Milagres was built in Monte.
Francisco de Vasconcelos Bettencourt had the chapel of Nossa Senhora das Virtudes built in São Martinho.
Francisco Homem de Couto built the Boa Morte chapel at Atouguia, Calheta.
Captain Manuel Telo de Meneses founded a Desterro chapel at Ribeira Grande, Machico.
The first stamped paper used in Madeira bore this date.
Miguel Achaioli wrote a manuscript genealogy of the Acciaioly family.
A corps of 100 artillerymen was created to defend Madeira's fortresses.
Diogo da Costa de Quintal built the chapel of Nossa Senhora das Angústias in Funchal.
Pedro Ferreira de Mesquita founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora dos Milagres at Ponta do Sol.
A deputy chief postmaster was appointed for Madeira, beginning regular postal service.
Canon Henrique Calaça de Viveiros died aged 73.
Endowment deed of the Conceição chapel in São Pedro founded by Rui Dias de Aguiar and his wife.
Inês Teixeira founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Vida at Fajã do Mar, Arco da Calheta.
A royal alvará raised the recolhimento of the Mercês at Calheta to a Poor Clare convent.
A royal charter concerning irrigation water in Madeira was issued.
The chapel of Nossa Senhora do Funchal at Ameixoeira, near Lisbon, was rebuilt and enlarged.
The church of Nossa Senhora do Calhau in Funchal was rebuilt between 1664 and 1688.
A hexagonal ten-réis stamp, overstamped with an armillary sphere and the provedor's signature, was used on stamped paper.
D. Mariana da Câmara obtained the office of fortificador of Madeira for her future son-in-law.
The Conselho da Fazenda granted 560$000 réis to enlarge the church of São Vicente.
A royal letter permitted the minting of gold and silver coin in Madeira.
Father Francisco de Castro died in Cape Verde.
Stamped paper was revalidated with a new date placed beside the old one.
Pope Alexander VII confirmed the elevation of the Mercês recolhimento to a convent.
João Fernandes Linhares founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Socorro at Canhas.
Land was bought for the new church of the Hospital de São Lázaro.
Manuel Tomás, aged 80, was murdered by a farrier's son.
D. Francisco de Mascarenhas was appointed governor of Madeira.
D. Francisco de Mascarenhas took office in Funchal as governor and captain-general of Madeira.
Funeral rites for Queen Luísa de Gusmão were held in Funchal at a cost of 192$300 réis.
Custódio Nunes da Costa built the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Boa Morte at the Cabo, Ponta do Pargo.
D. Francisco Manuel de Melo died.
The bones of many foundlings murdered by the foundling nurse were buried in the chapel of São Filipe.
The first women apparently entered the Recolhimento do Bom Jesus.
D. Mariana de Vasconcelos e Câmara Alencastre was donatary of Funchal.
The salary of the collegiate treasurer of Ribeira Brava was fixed.
Porto Santo was again raided and sacked; the parish church was sacked and later rebuilt, and archives were destroyed.
The Spanish consulate in Madeira was created.
Henrique Henriques de Noronha was born in Câmara de Lobos.
Manuel Gonçalves Lisboa founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Fé in São Martinho.
João da Paz de Castro built the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Rosário at Fundoa, São Roque.
The chapel of Santa Brígida was founded.
Gaspar Acciaioly died in Funchal.
A popular and ecclesiastical sedition, with nobles attacking the governor, broke out in Funchal and deposed, imprisoned and shipped off Governor D. Francisco de Mascarenhas.
Aires de Ornelas de Vasconcelos was elected governor and captain-general of Madeira after the deposition of Mascarenhas.
Aires de Saldanha de Sousa e Meneses was appointed governor of Madeira.
Norborough stayed in Madeira.
An alçada under João de Menezes Coutinho investigated the 1668 sedition against Mascarenhas.
Aires de Saldanha de Sousa e Meneses took office as governor of Madeira, ending Aires de Ornelas's interim governorship.
Lourenço de Matos Coutinho founded, in fulfilment of a vow, the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Quietação at Alecrins, Santo António.
D. Maria do Rosário de Arvelos reportedly built a chapel of Nossa Senhora da Penha de França at Lombada, Santa Cruz.
António Veloso de Lira was appointed canon of Funchal Cathedral.
Paintings signed by Nicolau Ferreira date from the late 17th century.
The Franciscan friary of Calheta was built from alms.
António de Carvalhal Esmeraldo founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Piedade at Jangão, Ponta do Sol.
The chapel of Nossa Senhora da Incarnação at Estreito de Câmara de Lobos was probably built, as dated over its portal.
The fraudulent Relation Historique de la découverte de l'isle de Madère, a French version of Alcoforado's account, was published in Paris.
D. Manuel Coutinho was born in Vila Nova de Anços.
Bishop Gabriel de Almeida governed the diocese of Funchal and approved the Recolhimento do Bom Jesus.

mentions.as_written: Março de 1671 a 13 de Julho de 1674

summary: D. Fr. Gabriel de Almeida, consecrated bishop of Funchal, took possession of the see, ending a 20-year vacancy.
The deed of endowment of the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Bom Despacho was signed.
João Saldanha de Albuquerque was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
João Saldanha de Albuquerque took office as governor of Madeira.
André de França e Andrade founded and built the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Conceição at Estreito da Calheta.
Further donations were made to the Recolhimento do Bom Jesus by Cidrão or his heirs.
Brites da Paixão professed at the Mercês convent.
A royal charter set the stipend of the vicar of Campanário at 19,000 réis plus grain and wine.
Bishop Gabriel de Almeida died in Funchal and was buried in the choir of the cathedral.
Pope Clement X confirmed D. Fr. António Teles da Silva as bishop of Funchal.
Ambrósio Vieira de Andrade built a chapel of St Francis in Santa Luzia.
An English translation of the account of Francisco Alcoforado was published in London.
Pedro Lopes de Vasconcelos founded the entail on which the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Saúde do Monte Olivete was built.
D. Fr. António Teles da Silva took charge of the diocese of Funchal.
The Conselho da Fazenda ordered a new parish church built at Tábua.
Francisco de Barros Maciel built the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Nazaré at Paredes, Arco da Calheta.
Morgado Aires de Ornelas built the Ornelas manor in Funchal.
Padre Matias Jorge Jardim founded a Rosary chapel in São Jorge.
Raul Esteves built a chapel of Nossa Senhora do Desterro at Ledo, Arco da Calheta.
The parish of Camacha was created and separated from Caniço, with its seat in the São Lourenço chapel, being definitively constituted in 1680.
Gonçalo de Freitas Drumond founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Pilar in São Martinho.
The diocese of Pernambuco was created, with the Madeiran D. Estêvão Brioso de Figueiredo presented as its bishop.
With the sugar trade in decline, a royal letter ordered 300 to 400 Madeiran couples to be transported to Brazil at state expense, making emigration government-promoted.
Alexandre de Moura e Albuquerque was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
Alexandre de Moura e Albuquerque took office as governor of Madeira.
The office of treasurer of the church of Caniço was abolished.

Following the prince regent's resolution of October 1676, royal charters of D. Pedro II dated 28 December 1676 created several new parishes and curacies, including Paul do Mar, Prazeres, Santa Luzia, Camacha, Serra de Água, Arco de São Jorge, Achadas da Cruz, Estreito and Arco da Calheta; collegiate benefices at Câmara de Lobos were abolished to fund some of them.
Lourenço de Matos Coutinho instituted the Alecrins entail.
The Conselho da Fazenda ordered the building of the chancel of Campanário church to be put out to tender.
Padre Manuel Ferreira da Silva was appointed first curate of Achadas da Cruz.
D. Estêvão Brioso de Figueiredo took possession of the see of Pernambuco.
Padre Cristóvão Vieira was appointed chaplain of the Curral das Freiras.
Bishop António da Silva Teles erected the parish of Serra de Água by episcopal provision.
Manuel Martins Brandão founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora das Brotas at Santo António, licensed for worship by alvará of July 1678.
The stipend of Seixal parish was reduced to 19$000 réis, a moio and a half of wheat and a pipe of wine.
Manuel Valente founded a chapel of Nossa Senhora da Vida in São Pedro parish.
The first edition of Fr. Rafael de Jesus's 'Castrioto Lusitano' was published in Lisbon.
Zenóbio de Medicis studied theology at Coimbra.
Luís Esmeraldo de Atouguia rebuilt the manor house at Lombada dos Esmeraldos.
A reference called the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Quietação the 'church of Alecrins'.
João de Brito was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
Licences fixed the annual stipends of the curate of Achadas da Cruz and the parish priest of Serra de Água.
João de Brito took office as governor of Madeira.
Bishop D. Fr. António Teles da Silva held a diocesan synod in Funchal.
Manuel Ribeiro Neto died.
The traveller Barbot visited Madeira.
The physician António de França Gomes founded the chapel of Saints Cosmas and Damian at Lombo do Salão, Calheta.
João Fernandes Vieira died in Olinda.
The endowment deed of the São José chapel in Porto Santo was signed.
A royal charter fixed the annual stipend of the first vicar of Santa Luzia.
Manuel Fernandes Gomes built the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Penha at Ferreiros, Calheta, and endowed it on 15 June 1682.
António Teles de Meneses, then living in Madeira, founded a chapel of Saint Anthony in Santa Maria Maior.
Four guards of the Santa Cruz customs were transferred to the Funchal customs.
The chapel of the Ilhéu fortress was built at some point between 1682 and 1692.
Padre Miguel Pereira endowed the chapel of São Miguel in the Jesuit College church of Funchal.
António de Sousa Torres was serving as Spanish consul in Funchal.
Bishop D. Frei António Teles da Silva died in Funchal.
A royal decree ordered the building of the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Conceição in the Ilhéu fortress at Funchal.
The old chapel of Nossa Senhora dos Varadouros was demolished to open the main gate in the Funchal city walls.
Prince Pedro informed the Funchal council of the death of King Afonso VI.
Lourenço da Costa founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Bom Sucesso at Lombo da Estrela, Calheta.
Padre Francisco da Cunha e Mendonça founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora das Preces at Câmara de Lobos.
Padre Manuel Gomes Garcês founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Livramento in São Vicente, erected by 1685.
Major repairs were carried out on the parish church of Machico in 1683, 1698 and 1713.
The parish church of Campanário was probably rebuilt, as the date on its façade suggests.
Domingos de Matos Cerveira investigated accusations against treasury officials in Madeira.
Pedro de Lima Brandão was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira and took office on 18 April 1684.
João Portes Homem founded the chapel of Santa Maria Madalena at Florenças, Arco da Calheta.
Inácio Ferreira Pinto had the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Livramento built at Monte.
D. Estêvão Brioso de Figueiredo was appointed bishop of Funchal and assumed government of the diocese in April 1685.
João Vieira de Afonseca built a chapel of São Francisco Xavier in Santa Cruz.
Maria de Aguiar founded a chapel of Nossa Senhora do Socorro at Estreito de Câmara de Lobos.
The new parish of Prazeres was installed in the chapel of Nossa Senhora dos Prazeres.
José Machado de Miranda became patron of a Madalena chapel and had it rebuilt.
Royal provisions transferred the administration of the lepers and of foundlings to the governor-general of Madeira.
Land on the Terreiro da Sé in Funchal was leased for a new Misericórdia hospital.
The endowment deed of the rock-cut chapel of Nossa Senhora da Penha de França at Faial was signed.
A judge-conservator of the tobacco monopoly existed in Madeira.
José de Seixas was serving as Spanish consul in Madeira.
The Santa Isabel hospital in Funchal was begun after this year.
The offices of quintador and clerk of the fifths at Calheta were abolished.
The 7th Count of Vimioso died.
The stipend of the vicar of Fajã da Ovelha was raised to 25,000 réis plus wheat and wine.
D. Lourenço de Almada was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
Dr Hans Sloane stayed in Madeira, recording armed merchants, the use of the corsa sledge and cases of syphilis.
Diogo Afonso de Aguiar founded a chapel in Tabua.
Death of the 1st Viscount of Fonte Arcada, as recorded in the entry on Pedro Joaquim de Magalhãis.
The Conselho da Fazenda authorised 900$000 réis for a new church at Monte, which was apparently never built.
D. Lourenço de Almada took office as governor and captain-general of Madeira, serving until 1690.
A decree abolished the fifth levied on sugars, replacing it with an eighth.
John Ovington called at Madeira on his voyage to Surat, noting the inhabitants' black clothing and their swords.
The Funchal city walls were completed under the governor D. Lourenço de Almada, and the Varadouros chapel was rebuilt above the new Portão dos Varadouros.
João Moniz da Silva was presented as bishop of Funchal but declined the appointment.
António Veloso de Lira was raised to magistral canon of Funchal Cathedral.
King Pedro II nominated Fr. José de Santa Maria bishop of Funchal. Pope Alexander VIII confirmed the appointment on 6 March 1690, and he was consecrated by Cardinal de Lencastre on 25 November 1690.
D. António Jorge de Melo was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira and took office on 27 April 1689.
D. Mariana de Alencastre, 9th donatary of Funchal, died.
On Easter night a great landslide, about half a league long, at Arco de São Jorge carried land into the sea, forming the Quebrada.
Bishop D. Estêvão Brioso de Figueiredo died in Lisbon.
The Conselho da Fazenda authorised payment of 1:007$000 réis for works on the Palácio de São Lourenço.
D. Rodrigo da Costa was appointed governor of Madeira and took office on 20 October 1690.
The chapel of São Cristóvão at Caramanchão, Machico, was built by the children of Cristóvão Moniz de Meneses under his will. The date 1692 is carved on its portico.
Canon Manuel Ferreira Teixeira founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora dos Remédios at Moreno, Santa Cruz (not in 1610, as had been claimed).
The Conselho da Fazenda ordered a new church to be built at Estreito da Calheta.
Two French corsairs sacked Porto Santo and robbed its church, destroying the parish archive.
Four sugar mills stood on the banks of the Ribeira de Santa Luzia.
The plane tree already grew in and around Funchal.
A fire destroyed nearly all the valuable archive of the Câmara Eclesiástica.
The present chapel of Santa Catarina in Funchal was rebuilt.
Canon António Espranger, the last of his family to occupy the Mosteiro Novo, died.
The last legal instrument concerning the donativo was issued.
Gaspar Berenguer de Andrade died.
Canon António Veloso de Lira died in Funchal and was buried in the cathedral chancel.
Bishop D. Fr. José de Santa Maria arrived in his diocese of Funchal.
Francisco Dias Franco founded a chapel of Nossa Senhora do Amparo in Machico.
The people of São Vicente built the chapel of São Vicente on a basalt rock at the mouth of the stream.
The Quinta das Cruzes chapel of Nossa Senhora da Piedade was built, endowed and inspected for worship.
The chapel of Nossa Senhora das Neves passed to D. Guiomar Castelo Branco.
Padre José de Andrade was appointed first chaplain of the chapel of the fortress of Nossa Senhora da Conceição do Ilhéu.
An order was issued for a new church at Estreito de Câmara de Lobos, contracted to Francisco Rodrigues.
Fr. Rafael de Jesus died.
D. Mécia was accidentally shot dead by a friar from the grounds of the São Francisco convent.
Superintendence of the Hospital de São Lázaro passed to the juiz de fora.
The Funchal municipal council took over superintendence of foundlings.
Manuel da Silva Pinheiro built the chapel of São Francisco Xavier at Cadeado, Lombo do Salão, Calheta, and endowed it by deed on 7 August 1693.
The remains of Padre Inácio Barbosa da Silva were moved to the Nazaré chapel at Arco da Calheta.
Pantaleão de Sá e Melo was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira and took office on 22 July 1694.
The Conselho da Fazenda ordered 651$000 réis for a new church at Água de Pena, probably never executed.
The deed of endowment of the chapel of Jesus-Maria-José at Câmara de Lobos was executed.
A deed of donation was made for the Piedade chapel and worship began there; its portal is dated 1692.
Pedro de Sousa Maciel was master gunner of the fort of São Roque at Machico.
Pedro Júlio da Câmara Leme was born.
The parish church of Tábua was probably completed, as the date on its façade inscription indicates.
The Anunciação chapel at Lombo dos Canhas was rebuilt; it later served as the parish church.
John Ovington's 'A voyage to Suratt' was published in London.
The endowment deed of the chapel of Santo António da Malvasia was made, the chapel being founded that year.
Bishop D. Fr. José de Santa Maria left Madeira and relinquished the administration of the diocese.
The Diocesan Seminary was installed in the Mosteiro Novo in Funchal.
King Pedro II appointed José de Sousa Castelo Branco bishop of Funchal.
Canon Pedro Correia Barbosa founded the chapel of São Francisco das Furnas in São Pedro parish.
Manuel Mendes Serrão is recorded as a familiar of the Holy Office.
Manuel Telo Catanho de Meneses was honorary captain of the Fortaleza de São Tiago.
Pedro Correia Barbosa preached a panegyric sermon to St Anthony at the feast of the Funchal Cathedral chapter.
Manuel Rodrigues was born in Funchal.
Fr. Francisco de Santa Teresa died.
A provision announced a new tobacco administration in Madeira from 1699.
The present parish church of Santana was built at government expense.
Bartolomeu de Sá Machado built or rebuilt the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Amparo at Álamos.
The first master gunner of the Ilhéu fort was appointed.
A curacy was reportedly created in Campanário.
The Conselho da Fazenda ordered the completion of works on the parish church of Serra de Água.
José de Sousa Castelo Branco was consecrated bishop in Lisbon.
Bishop José de Sousa Castelo Branco arrived at Mazagão to perform episcopal duties.
Bishop José de Sousa Castelo Branco arrived in Funchal to take up his diocese.
The precentor Domingos de Andrade e Alvarenga built the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Graça in the Sé parish.
Pedro Correia Barbosa published his panegyric sermon to St Anthony.
A protective wall was built for the Faial chapel against floods.
D. Manuel Coutinho took his doctorate in theology at Coimbra.
The parish church of Serra de Água was substantially enlarged.
Manuel Gomes Ferreira was brought from Setúbal to Madeira as fortificador.
D. Francisco de Mascarenhas died.
A fire broke out in the houses of São Lourenço in Funchal.
The chapel at Ribeira da Janela, built by the people, received its endowment, probably marking its first construction.
Flood waters entered the old church of Faial and carried away the body of the Rei Pequeno from his tomb.
Filipe de Carvalhal Esmeraldo administered the Santo Amaro entail.
Clipped money in Madeira was ordered withdrawn and 80,000 cruzados in new coin were sent.
The parish of Prazeres was suppressed and reattached to Estreito da Calheta.
The chapel of St John at Câmara de Lobos was endowed by public deed.
Canon António Lopes de Andrade built and endowed the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Conceição at São Roque.
Father Francisco Valhadolid died in the parish of Santos, Lisbon, and was buried in its church.
An edict of the provedor required all goods to be landed at the customs redoubt in Funchal.
The fort of Caniçal was built after pirates landed there.
The Oliveira family house in Rua da Cadeia Velha, Funchal, was probably built.
The Espírito Santo chapel at Lombada dos Esmeraldos was rebuilt.
The Bânger pillar stood on a reef reached by canoe from the city wall.
Domingos de Oliveira Álvares settled in Funchal as a wine merchant.
A curacy was created in the parish of Fajã da Ovelha as its population grew.
A new parish church replaced the São Lourenço chapel at Fajã da Ovelha.
A flood destroyed the Calheta municipal archive.
Dr Heberden, visiting Madeira, estimated average life expectancy on the island at 39 years.
João José Bettencourt de Freitas rebuilt the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Livramento at Monte.
According to tradition, a ship wrecked at Funchal brought the first Figueira da Índia to Madeira.
The fort of São João da Pontinha was built on the second islet at Funchal, linking it to land.
Holy Spirit impérios were held in every street of Funchal, marked by gluttony and drunkenness.
The síndico of the Funchal senate often replaced the council clerk, drafting and signing the minutes.

mentions.as_written: fins do século XVIII e princípios do século XIX

summary: The Sarsfield surname was apparently introduced into Madeira.
The Madre de Deus chapel at Tabua was destroyed by the nearby stream.
São Vicente was raised to a town, the only one on the north coast.
Traditional dating of the cave collapse that killed D. Cosme de Medicis and his friends.
Vinhático timber was exported to England as Madeira mahogany.
José Phelps came to Madeira as a merchant.
A Norwegian ship was wrecked near the Pontinha, bringing the young Luiz Henriques to Madeira.
Outeiros poetic gatherings took place in Funchal.
D. Guiomar Madalena Acciaioly lived in Funchal and had her goods seized for debts.

mentions.as_written: fins do século XVIII e princípios do XIX

summary: La Peyrouse visited Madeira and noted the phosphorescence of its seas.
João Manuel's early two-storey house was still standing, owned by António do Carvalhal.
The chapel of Santa Isabel in the Funchal Misericórdia building was probably built.
The chapel of Nossa Senhora da Consolação at Caniço was rebuilt.
The parish church of Ponta Delgada was considerably enlarged.
Eusébio da Silva Barros founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Boa Nova at São Gonçalo.
The provedor da Fazenda was allowed to summon militia officers and soldiers as witnesses without the governor's leave.
João da Costa de Ataíde e Azevedo was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
João da Costa de Ataíde e Azevedo took office as governor and captain-general of Madeira.
A charter reduced the municipal election of militia officers to mere recommendation.
D. Rodrigo da Costa was appointed governor of Bahia.
Diogo Sálter de Macedo investigated conflicts between the bishop, the governor and the provedor in Madeira.
Duarte Sodré Pereira was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
Governor João da Costa de Ataíde e Azevedo died in Funchal.
Duarte Sodré Pereira took office as governor of Madeira.
The Conselho da Fazenda ordered the new church and sacristy of São Roque to be put out to tender for 795$000 réis.
Governor Duarte Sodré revalued the coins circulating in Madeira.
Inácio Viana do Rego built the chapel of Santo António at the Quinta de Santo António, Estreito de Câmara de Lobos.
Teodoro de Pavia's book «Il Primo Scuoprimento dell'isola di Madera» was published at Tortona, Italy.
A charter of the regent Infanta D. Catarina authorised building a new parish church at Fajã da Ovelha on a more suitable site.
The regent D. Catarina approved moving the new church of Estreito da Calheta to another site.
Licence was granted to bless the new Madre de Deus chapel at Estreito de Câmara de Lobos.
King Pedro II died, an event commemorated in sonnets by Francisco de Vasconcelos Coutinho.
The fort of Nossa Senhora do Amparo was built.
A flood damaged the church of Nossa Senhora do Calhau in Funchal and much of its churchyard.
Construction of the Fort of São Pedro in Funchal, ordered by Duarte Sodré Pereira, was completed, according to an inscription on its gate.
Hans Sloane's Voyage, including his impressions of Madeira, was published in London.
D. Rodrigo da Costa was appointed viceroy of India.
A flood caused considerable damage across Madeira.
D. João V instituted the new ordenanças (militia).
Probable construction of the Preces chapel in Santo António.
The fort of São João Baptista at Machico was built; the fort of Porto da Cruz is also dated to this year.
French pirates raided and sacked Porto Santo, burning the parish church and some houses.
D. Fr. José de Santa Maria, former bishop of Funchal, died in Porto as its bishop.
The Jesus-Maria-José chapel at Lombo do Doutor, Calheta, was founded and endowed by public deed.
Gaspar Mendes de Vasconcelos had a new marble tombstone with inscription made for Martim Mendes de Vasconcelos in the church of Santa Clara.
Luís Gonçalves da Silva founded the São José chapel at Ribeira Brava.
Henrique Henriques de Noronha wrote the Árvore dos Henriques.
The people built a chapel of the Souls in the churchyard of Estreito de Câmara de Lobos parish church.
Manuel Pestana Teixeira and his wife founded the Boa Viagem chapel at Carne Azeda, inspected for worship on 28 June 1711.
D. Frei João do Nascimento took a doctorate in canon law at Coimbra.
Inácio Gomes Fragoso became engineer of fortifications in Madeira.
D. Pedro Alvares da Cunha was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
D. Luísa de Mendonça founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Amparo in São Martinho.
The Penha de França fort and chapel in Funchal were built or rebuilt.
D. Pedro Alvares da Cunha took office as governor of Madeira.
D. Frei João do Nascimento entered the Franciscan seminary of Varatojo.
João de Vasconcelos Uzel was appointed captain of the Porto da Cruz fort.
Earliest known document concerning the official who struck the hours at Funchal Cathedral.
The Socorro hermitage at Porto da Cruz was built.
João de Aguiar built the chapel of Santo António at the Funchal Customs House.
Manuel Rodrigues enlisted in a regiment bound for Colónia do Sacramento.
João de Saldanha da Gama was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira on 4 May 1715 and took office on 27 June.
Bishop José de Sousa de Castelo Branco left Madeira.
Poems by Francisco de Vasconcelos Coutinho were included in the Fenix renascida.
D. João V renewed the title of Marquess of Valença for the 8th Count of Vimioso.
The first edition of the Historia Insulana was published.
Manuel Ferreira Teixeira entailed the Selvagens Islands.
Captain Manuel Rodrigues Ferreira Ferro died and was buried in his Blessed Sacrament chapel at Porto Moniz.
Henrique Henriques de Noronha wrote the Non plus ultra da Nobreza.
Owing to illness, Bishop D. José de Sousa Castelo Branco left Madeira for Portugal, never to return.
João de Saldanha da Gama's governorship ended; the Santa Clara nuns performed a farewell play and Francisco de Vasconcelos Coutinho wrote a eulogy.
The Santo António chapel at Monte was erected.
Jorge Martins de Sousa e Meneses was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira on 1 June 1718 and took office on 5 October.
Manuel Rodrigues took his vows in the Franciscan order.
A royal charter ordered a new parish church to be built at Santa Luzia.
The state rebuilt the São João da Ribeira chapel after a flood destroyed it.
John Atkins visited Madeira.
The ruined Espírito Santo chapel at Câmara de Lobos, founded by Zarco, was rebuilt.
D. José de Sousa Castelo Branco resigned the bishopric of Funchal.
An image of Santa Quitéria was donated to the church of Ponta Delgada.
Sauvaire, French consul-general in Madeira, wrote a letter on the volcanic island that appeared near São Miguel.
The chapel of São Gonçalo was built.
D. Rodrigo da Costa died.
Padre António Cordeiro died in Lisbon.
King João V nominated D. Manuel Coutinho bishop of Funchal.
D. Francisco Júlio de Oliveira was appointed bishop of Funchal but did not take possession.
Dr Julião Fernandes da Silva was born in Funchal.
Nicolau Francisco Xavier da Silva published Puro e affectuoso sacrificio in Lisbon.
A royal letter removed games, dances and figures from the Corpus Christi procession, except St George.
The Santa Quitéria chapel at Lombo da Estrela, Calheta, was built and its deed of endowment signed.
The deed of endowment of the Santo António chapel at Arco da Calheta, built in 1724, was executed.
Francisco da Costa Freire was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
Francisco da Costa Freire took office as governor of Madeira.
A flood devastated Machico, killing 26 people and razing over 80 houses.
Funchal merchants petitioned the Senate on the wine trade and the entry of north-coast wine.
Governor Francisco da Costa Freire founded the Recolhimento das Órfãs in Funchal with four orphans.
Nicolau Francisco Xavier da Silva took his doctorate in canon law at Coimbra.
Governor Francisco da Costa Freire arrested two councillors over precedence in the Corpus Christi procession.
The Holy See confirmed D. Manuel Coutinho as bishop of Funchal after delays caused by disputes with Rome.
D. Manuel Coutinho was consecrated bishop by Patriarch Tomaz de Almeida.
Bishop D. Manuel Coutinho arrived in Funchal and took charge of the diocese.
Manuel de Carvalho Valdavesso built the chapel of São Luís at Diferença, Faial, and its deed of endowment was executed.
Afonso Caminha de Vasconcelos e Sousa received the captaincy of Funchal.
The São Pedro chapel at Lamaceiros was recorded as badly ruined.
The deed of endowment was made for the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Boa Hora above Funchal.
António Vogado endowed the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Vale by public deed.
Bishop D. Manuel Coutinho established a provisional curacy in the chapel at Ribeira da Janela.
São Vicente was raised to a town, the first new town in Madeira since the early 16th century.
The chapel of Santo António da Mouraria was erected.
A royal charter fixed the stipend of the Campanário curate at 20,000 réis, and the post was filled.
The deed of endowment of the Santa Quitéria chapel at Pico do Cardo was signed.
D. Filipe de Alarcão e Mascarenhas was appointed governor of Madeira, taking office on 27 September.
Padre João Betencourt da Câmara founded the chapel of St John the Baptist in Campanário.
Jorge Martins de Sousa e Meneses died.
The chapel of Nossa Senhora da Piedade at Monte was founded and endowed.
Francisco de Vasconcelos Coutinho's Feudo do Parnaso and Hecatombe metrico were published in Lisbon.
Santana parishioners obtained leave to rebuild the chapel of Santo António at Achada de Santo António, which was rebuilt and inspected ahead of its blessing in April 1730.
D. Lourenço de Almada died.
Troilo de Vasconcelos da Cunha died in Lisbon.
The date 1730 inscribed over the portico probably marks the building of the church of the Porciúncula convent at Ribeira Brava.
João do Couto Cardoso founded the Piedade chapel at Jardim do Mar.
Padre António Gonçalves Franco founded the São José chapel in Machico.
The main sacristy and chapter house of Funchal Cathedral were built.
Henrique Henriques de Noronha died.
The people of Boaventura built the chapel of Santa Quitéria at Serrão.
Francisco Aurélio da Câmara Leme married Antónia Maria Acciaioli de Vasconcelos Bettencourt.
Major repairs were carried out on the Madalena chapel in 1732, 1766 and 1773.
Manuel Rodrigues published numerous sermons and discourses in Lisbon.
The Funchal council asked that its members be immune from arrest by civil and church authorities.
Canon Francisco Cândido Correia Henriques built and endowed the chapel of São Cândido at Fonte da Rocha, Câmara de Lobos.
A contract worth 3,050,000 réis was made for building the great sacristy and chapter house of Funchal Cathedral.
Manuel Rodrigues de Canha built a chapel dedicated to Nossa Senhora and Santana at Outeiro.
A royal charter formally created the curacy of Ribeira da Janela.
King João V authorised the creation of a curacy at Boaventura.
Major works on the Funchal customs building were ordered.
João de Abreu Castelo Branco was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
A charter created the curacy of Prazeres, separating it from Estreito da Calheta and making it dependent on Paul do Mar.
The ruined and profaned chapel of São Sebastião at Ponta do Sol was rebuilt at the municipal council's expense and inspected for divine offices on 20 November 1734.
João de Abreu Castelo Branco took office as governor of Madeira.
The deed of endowment of the Rosary chapel at Campanário was signed.
The rebuilt chapel of Nossa Senhora da Piedade at Porto da Cruz was licensed for blessing.
An alvará of King João V created the curacy of Jardim do Mar.
The last Antwerp edition of Dr António da Gama's Decisiones appeared.
A mandate confirmed the power of Madeira's provedor da fazenda to arrest persons without the corregedor's licence.
The old parish church of São Martinho was almost entirely rebuilt.
Madeira began importing sugar from abroad, marking the decline of its own sugar production.
The smaller organ of Funchal Cathedral was acquired.
Pedro José de Faria Bettencourt was administrator of the entail seated at the Brotas chapel.
The chapel of Nossa Senhora da Piedade at Jardim do Mar was founded.
The naturalist Daniel Carlos Solander was born in Nordland.
An alvará fixed the stipend of Manuel do Nascimento, curate of Jardim do Mar.
A certified copy of the 1515 charter was extracted from the Livro das Ilhas.
The chapel of Nossa Senhora das Maravilhas, rebuilt by Mariana da Silva, was inspected for the celebration of Mass.
A new parish church of São Pedro, Funchal, was built by contract.
The Funchal Senate issued an ordinance banning north-coast wines from the town.
Francisco Pedro de Meneses Gorjão was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira.
Francisco Pedro de Meneses Gorjão took office as governor of Madeira in Funchal.
Works for a new church at Monte were put out to tender for 6.742$000 réis.
Padre Augusto de Góis is recorded as a familiar of the Holy Office.
The ruined chapel of São Roque at Machico was rebuilt by its confraternity on its present site, and licence for its blessing was granted on 6 June 1739.
A law granted the style of excelência to great churchmen and to captains-general within their governments.
The Conselho de Fazenda ordered the building of a new parish church at Arco de São Jorge.
George Anson's squadron of eight ships called at Madeira on its way to the Pacific.
Frei João do Nascimento was appointed bishop of Funchal by João V, confirmed by Pope Benedict XIV on 5 January 1741, and consecrated on 5 May 1741.
Francisco João Róscio was born in Madeira.
The new church of Santa Luzia was presumably completed.
Padre António Ribeiro de Sousa is recorded as a familiar of the Holy Office.
Bishop Manuel Coutinho left Madeira for the mainland following his appointment to Lamego.
The foundation stone of the new Monte church was laid after the old chapel was demolished.
José da Costa Torres, later bishop, was born in Setúbal.
Bishop Frei João do Nascimento arrived in Madeira.
The stipend of the beneficiaries of Machico was commuted.
A royal order denied the Funchal council authority over ships.
Bishop Manuel Coutinho died at Soure on his way to Lamego.
A curacy was established in the parish of Tábua.
São Vicente was raised to a town and municipality, separated from Machico and taking in Porto Moniz.
The office of alcaide do mar at the Santa Cruz customs house was abolished.
João Moniz de Abreu was hired as fortificador for Madeira's fortifications.
The new parish church of Arco de São Jorge, dedicated to São José, was blessed.

A royal charter raised the parish of São Vicente to the status of a town and municipality, attaching northern localities such as Porto Moniz, Ponta Delgada and Seixal to it and further reducing the municipality of Machico.
The contract for building the new parish church of Arco da Calheta was awarded.
Construction of the new church of Faial was awarded to Cristóvão Gomes.
Father Manuel de Nóbrega founded and endowed the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Esperança at Vale Formoso.
A memorial stone to the Jesuit martyrs led by Inácio de Azevedo was erected at Pico do Cardo.
The sacristy and bell-tower of Santana church were built.
Thomas Nichols's description of Madeira was published in Astley's collection.
Francisco Newton founded the wine house later known as Cossart, Gordon & Co.
The works on the new church of Prazeres were put out to contract for 4,100$000 réis.
A last decree fixed the stipend of the beneficiaries of Ribeira Brava parish.
A new church for Água de Pena was ordered, for 4:000$000 réis, on a less windy site.
The first stone of the new church of Faial was blessed.
A royal charter created a curacy in the parish of Santa Luzia.
Death of the former bishop D. José de Sousa Castelo Branco.
Major repairs costing 1,200$000 réis were carried out on the Convento das Mercês.
A royal letter created a curacy in Faial whose curate had to serve the chapel of São Roque.
Francisco João de Vasconcelos Bettencourt was admitted to the Assembleia dos Únicos do Funchal and delivered an academic oration.
A tabernacle with the Blessed Sacrament was requested for the church of Tábua.
The new church of Nossa Senhora do Monte was declared complete.
The Treasury Council authorised payments in 1747, 1751 and 1754 for building the new church of São Jorge.
Dr Thomas Heberden made the first meteorological observations in Madeira, at Funchal.
A royal letter asked the captain-general to assist emigration from Madeira to Brazil.
The Conselho da Fazenda awarded the contract to build the new church of Fajã da Ovelha to the carpenter Francisco Gomes.
Bishop D. Frei João do Nascimento was appointed governor of Madeira, governing the archipelago until 1751.
Governor Francisco Pedro de Meneses Gorjão left Madeira to govern Maranhão.
João Francisco Lopes Rocha was born in the Sé parish of Funchal.
A royal charter ordered the building of walls along the ribeiras at Santa Cruz.
The Episcopal Palace of Funchal was built at a cost of twenty contos de réis.
Francisco Xavier de Ornelas, a founder of the Arcadia Funchalense, was born.
Conventional end of Madeira's sugar-making period; according to Dr Azevedo, the industry disappeared owing to American competition.
The chapel of São Cristóvão at Ponta Delgada was demolished.
The Rosary chapel at Campanário was inspected and opened for worship.
Domingos Rodrigues Martins succeeded as fortificador of Madeira.

On the night of 31 March to 1 April 1748 a violent earthquake struck Madeira, causing few deaths but heavy damage to buildings, including the cathedral, the bishops' palace, the customs house, the Monte church, the Mosteiro Novo house and numerous chapels and parish churches.

summary: Padre Inácio Barbosa da Silva bequeathed houses for a hospital of the Misericórdia of Machico.
A royal charter ordered the building of river walls at Machico.
A royal charter authorised 2,450$000 réis for building a new church at Porto da Cruz.
Dr Julião Fernandes da Silva completed his medical degree at Coimbra.
A confraternity to support the Hospital of São Lázaro was authorised.
The chapel of Nossa Senhora das Vitórias was built in Machico.
Death of the 8th Count of Vimioso.
According to Heberden, 1749 and 1750 were very dry years in Madeira.
The Fort of São Francisco was built in Santa Cruz, funded by fines on militiamen who missed lookout duty.
D. João V pardoned the finto tax owed for 1739–1749.
The foundation stone of the new Caniçal church was laid.
The stipend of the vicar of São Pedro was raised to 60,000 réis.
The stipend of the priest of Serra de Água was confirmed without increase.
The chapel of Nossa Senhora da Graça in Machico was rebuilt by its confraternity.
Bishop D. Frei João do Nascimento founded the Confraria dos Escravos de Nossa Senhora do Monte.
Pecunia Insulana copper coins bearing Funchal's original arms were struck for circulation only in Madeira and the Azores.
An English account of the discovery and present state of Madeira, an abridged version of Alcoforado's narrative attributed to Dr Johns, was published in London.
Canon Agostinho de Góis e Meneses founded the chapel of Nossa Senhora das Preces at Machico.
Heberden recorded shade temperatures of up to 25° during the leste wind.
Papal briefs were granted for private oratories in the parish of Estreito da Calheta.
Tomé João Pimenta rebuilt the chapel of São João Baptista at Lombo de São João, Ribeira Brava.
A royal alvará granted one conto de réis for repairs and a new choir at the Convent of the Incarnação.
Licence was granted to bless the São José chapel at Ribeira Brava.
The endowment deed of the chapel of Nossa Senhora do Monte at Ponta do Sol was signed.
The new church of Caniçal was solemnly blessed.
Manuel de Santana e Vasconcelos lived in the second half of the eighteenth century.
Dr Heberden gave the first favourable account of Madeira's climate.
A measles epidemic caused notable mortality in Madeira; Dr Thomas Heberden gave excellent service during it in Funchal.
Rodrigo da Costa Almeida held the post of capitão-cabo of the Fortress of Pico.
Bernardo da Gama was captain of the Fort of São Jorge at Calheta.
The old episcopal palace of Funchal was built.
The chapel of Nossa Senhora do Monte at Lombo das Terças, Ponta do Sol, was built by local people, and licence to bless it was granted on 15 September 1751.
The date 1751 was inscribed on the high altar of the Chapel of São Roque, Machico, perhaps marking a new altar.
D. José I was acclaimed king in Funchal.
Padre José Lopes wrote that the chapel was dedicated to St Quitéria.
D. Álvaro José Xavier Botelho de Távora was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira and took office on 27 August 1751.
The foundation stone of the parish church of Prazeres was laid and blessed.
Francisco Aurélio da Câmara Leme rebuilt the Chapel of São Filipe and the manor house at Quinta do Leme, Santo António.
The Funchal council resolved to demolish the old chapel of St James and build a larger church, completed in 1768.
A royal charter gave Madeiran foundling wet-nurses the privileges of those in Lisbon.
Tithes beyond the clergy's upkeep were secularised.
Vitúrio Lopes Rocha was born in Funchal.
Hans Sloane died in Chelsea.
The second edition of Espelho de Lusitanos by António Veloso de Lira appeared.
Gunners' daily pay at the Fortress of São Lourenço rose from 30 to 80 réis.
The foundation stone of the new parish church of Estreito de Câmara de Lobos was laid.
The Council of the Treasury authorised building a new parish church in Gaula.
Bishop D. Frei João do Nascimento died in Funchal (one entry gives 26 November).
Funeral rites for D. João V were held in Funchal Cathedral.
A French astronomical commission made observations in Funchal and was attacked by the populace.
Nuno de Freitas da Silva rebuilt the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Conceição at Ponta Delgada.
Services were still held in the Chapel of Santa Brígida.
Captain-general Manuel Saldanha da Gama Albuquerque reported on the poor state of the militias.
A list of British merchants active in Funchal is recorded.
Captain Roque João Acciaioly was master gunner of the Fort of São Filipe da Praça.
The Fort of Santo António at Paul do Mar was built.
Manuel Saldanha da Gama Albuquerque was appointed governor and captain-general of Madeira and took office on 16 May 1754.
Licence was granted to bless the enlarged chapel at Ribeira da Janela.
D. Álvaro José Xavier Botelho de Távora left the governorship of Madeira.
Nicolau Francisco Xavier da Silva died in Lisbon.
Riots broke out in Calheta, Ponta do Sol and São Vicente over a concession of Paul da Serra.
Major repairs to the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Penha de França were paid for by the faithful.
De Bory visited Madeira aboard the Cometa.
The new parish church of Arco da Calheta was solemnly blessed.
Aires José Maria de Saldanha, 2nd Count of Ega, son of the governor, was born in Funchal and baptised on 27 May in the chapel of the São Lourenço palace.
Fr. João de São José wrote his letter to Dr Julião Fernandes da Silva, and the Carta critica closed on 7 September 1755.
The great earthquake struck Portugal and caused sea movements on Madeira's coast.
The Chapel of the Blessed Sacrament in Funchal Cathedral was demolished and rebuilt.
Joaquim Leonardo da Rocha was born in Portugal.
The book "The Affecting" was published in London.
Episcopal visitor António Mendes de Almeida inspected the chapel of Santo António in Curral das Freiras.
The office overseeing Madeira's fortifications began to be held by trained military engineers.
The chancel of the new church of Estreito de Câmara de Lobos was blessed.
A royal letter ordered the construction of a harbour of refuge in Funchal.
Pope Benedict XIV confirmed Gaspar Afonso da Costa Brandão as bishop of Funchal.
